author: Example Security Team
audience: The security lead, service owners, and engineering teams
recipients: Example Client security lead and authorized service owners
objectives: Identify actionable configuration weaknesses in the approved customer portal endpoints
business_context: The customer portal supports account access and service requests. Protecting session identifiers and maintaining reliable access are the primary business concerns.
priority_assets: The approved login endpoint and its session-handling controls are the priority. The payment service remains excluded.
methodology: The assessment used bounded unauthenticated HTTP response review, TLS certificate checks, and a single TCP connectivity check. The professional reviewed every reported finding and assigned its severity.
limitations: The work did not include authenticated user roles, business-logic testing, exploitation, application source review, or comprehensive cipher enumeration. A failed legacy TLS probe was inconclusive under the local client policy.
delivery_method: The approved encrypted client delivery portal
evidence_policy: Report sanitized header observations and short validation notes. Do not retain passwords, bearer tokens, session cookie values, or customer records.
remediation_context: Service owners should agree deployment dates and arrange targeted validation after changes. The proposed dates below are planning targets supplied for this example.
executive_context: Two configuration findings require remediation planning: a session cookie without the Secure attribute and a missing Content Security Policy on the selected HTML response. Neither observation demonstrates account compromise. The recommendations focus on transport protection and browser defense in depth.
